title: Prefix cache async iterator stall leading to memory leak — action plan and mitigations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: After a capacity event on dedicated clusters we observed unbounded memory growth on several prefix cache shards. Investigation traced the issue to an async prefetch iterator used by the prefix cache read-path which retained references when upstream RPC contexts were canceled; those ghost entries bypassed eviction heuristics and accumulated until OOMs and eviction storms occurred.
production_impact: Capacity surge on dedicated hosts: transient 5-15% tail latency increase for generation routes and three pod OOM restarts during 2026-02-09 incident window. A small subset of customers on dedicated pools experienced degraded throughput for ~40 minutes while mitigations rolled out.
root_cause_summary: An async iterator created by the prefix cache prefetcher did not unregister itself when the parent request was cancelled. The iterator kept strong references to KV entries and internal slab objects, preventing eviction score decay and compaction from reclaiming memory. Under load this resulted in ghost-entry accumulation and backpressure that amplified eviction churn.
links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5068 -- longer-term: iterator refactor + weakrefs and backpressure
comments: 2026-02-09 03:12 UTC — Oncall alerted: prefixcache memory alert fired for dedicated-us-east-1 pool. Initial mitigation: increase eviction aggressiveness and scale out shard replicas.
2026-02-09 03:28 UTC — Scoped impact: three pods OOM'd. Ramp-up mitigation: temporarily disable prefetch for heavy-tenancy prefixes via feature flag.
2026-02-09 04:05 UTC — Debugging: heap profiles collected and compared; observed retained objects tied to 'prefetch_iterator' frames. Opened ENG-732911 to track follow-up.

2026-02-10 10:40 UTC — Root cause workshop with runtime, infra, and reliability. Decided two-track remediation: (A) urgent hotfix to guarantee cancellation/unregister semantics, (B) medium-term iterator refactor with weak references and prefetch backpressure.
2026-02-16 16:22 UTC — Hotfix PR merged (5023). Released as runtime-1.20.2 to hosted and dedicated pools. Oncall confirmed mitigations reduced memory retention within 30 minutes of rollout.

2026-02-24 11:03 UTC — Design review for long-term fix completed. Trade-offs discussed: weakref complexity vs explicit lifecycle management. Chosen approach: explicit lifecycle with safeties and metrics, plus optional weakref guard as a belt-and-suspenders.

2026-03-02 09:45 UTC — PR 5068 opened implementing refactor, new telemetry counters (iterator-allocs, iterator-cancellations, ghost-entry-count), and a canary rollout plan. Requesting runtime and infra reviews.
2026-03-04 15:10 UTC — Security and compliance confirmed no customer data exposure. Decided no separate security review required (variations of existing code paths).

2026-03-05 12:32 UTC — Draft runbook updates committed: detection alerts, emergency feature-flag toggles, heap collection instructs, and rollback steps for runtime changes. Moving ticket to In Progress to track remaining action items.

A-2: Add telemetry and alerts for 'ghost-entry-count' and iterator cancellation mismatch — owner: Lina Morales (Reliability) — estimate: 3 — due: 2026-03-10
A-3: Add a feature-flagged prefetch backpressure mechanism (max in-flight prefetch per shard) and test in canary — owner: Samir Bose — estimate: 5 — due: 2026-03-22
A-4: Update runbooks and incident playbook sections related to prefix cache memory alerts, include heap snapshot collection steps — owner: Aisha Patel — estimate: 2 — due: 2026-03-12
A-5: Post-deploy chaos test to simulate high cancelation rates and verify no regrowth of ghost entries — owner: Chaos Engineering — estimate: 3 — due: 2026-03-25

A-6: Customer communication: prepare note for Dedicated customers who saw impact with mitigation timeline and what changed — owner: Customer Success (draft by Marco Nguyen) — estimate: 1 — due: 2026-03-14
followups: F-1: Audit other async iterators in runtime codebase for similar cancellation leaks (cross-team code owners pinged)
F-2: Schedule a 90-day postmortem follow-up to confirm no recurrence and validate new telemetry thresholds
F-3: Consider adding automatic eviction-of-ghost-entries sweep if iterator anomalies detected for >1h
F-4: Feed findings into prefix-cache redesign evaluation (performance vs memory-safety trade-offs)
